name: @veyq/core-js
//: The Kotlin core's modules (src/mobile/core, apps/*, composition) compiled for JavaScript, ADR 0155 decisions 3, 6 and 7.1: Gradle compiles (`build`, which runs `:composition:jsPackage` and writes `dist/` — one file per module, Kotlin's per-module names, the platform's `kotlin_veyq_mobile_core.mjs`, and one `.d.mts` for every module's exports, `veyq-mobile-composition.d.mts`; never committed), pnpm installs, bundles and tests. Its primitives are the web's own @noble/*, at @veyq/crypto's ranges so the lockfile holds one version of each. Its check runs the suite's conformance over contracts/crypto/vectors/v1.json under Node, from a binary of its own (`dist/conformance/`), never an export of the shipped module; each façade's vectors through the shipped module; and the slice check (`src/slice.test.ts`): the bundle an entry ships carries no kotlinx.serialization, coroutines, Ktor or NotOnTheWeb source, within ADR 0155's budget. One entry per façade (ADR 0155 decision 5), each a file of its own that `:composition:jsPackage` writes beside the module file holding the façade (`dist/<entry>.mjs` and `.d.mts`, re-exporting exactly the façade's `@JsExport` declarations, read from its sources), never the composition's own (an empty shell), so a name of one façade does not resolve through another's entry: `./search`, the platform's search, and `./tree`, the platform's node tree rules, both from `kotlin_veyq_mobile_core.mjs`. `sideEffects: false`: the compiled module imports Ktor's client for its engine's registration (an eager initializer) though no façade reaches Ktor, so a bundler may drop what nothing uses.

scripts.check: pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test
